digest.component_or_area: RP-04 architecture — secrets and authentication design
propositions: Rebar must support multiple credential sources (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gerrit, GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Jira) across local, CI, AWS, CLI, library, MCP, and hosted contexts without a universal secret broker or hand-rolled credential store.

Static credentials must rotate by process restart/redeploy; no hot-reload, file-watcher, environment-poll, or runtime credential-refresh subsystem is introduced; native temporary/workload credentials remain SDK-owned.

Provider-native authentication capabilities (boto3 Session, Anthropic AccessTokenProvider, OpenAI workload identity) are injected into Rebar-owned factories; unavoidable static values use non-serializable Pydantic SecretStr/SecretBytes containers inside provider-specific adapters only.

Subprocess children inherit the ambient environment for compatibility; Rebar overlays static credentials only onto the owning adapter's child; exact sibling-secret variable names are removed from unrelated children; global os.environ is never mutated.

Deployment resolves external secret stores (SSM, vaults) before startup and supplies one key via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH (file, preferred) or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY (multiline env); Rebar validates, materializes to 0600-file in a 0700-directory, and binds context-locally without global mutation.
Operation snapshots are structurally non-secret; credential/client/auth values are excluded from snapshots, caches, fingerprints, MCP arguments, CLI args, logs, and error representations.
